sub_scenario.family: physical constraint versus sustained work commitment
sub_scenario.one_line: field geologist: plateau first for the staged ascent

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the sampling plan and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The expedition calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Low-altitude campaigns of any length are physically uneventful for me.
Altitude is the only variable that matters.
The only one on my chart.
Someone new shadowed me in the field station this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the ascent profiles into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
On the last high-plateau survey I staged two acclimatization nights on the way up, and I logged full sampling days at four thousand meters with clean data and no symptoms.
The staged protocol held under real work.
Held for three straight weeks.
Even at elevation, short summit days after proper staging have been fine.
Staged exposure works at any intensity.
So far without exception.
I archived last cycle's notes on the expedition calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
My altitude physician recommends staged ascent with two overnight stops for any work above three thousand five hundred meters.
A written staging protocol.
Written after my one bad episode years ago.
A vendor call about the sampling plan ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the field station checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the ascent profiles.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the expedition calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
Two spring campaigns are open: the plateau campaign builds the two staged nights into its logistics, while the canyon campaign helicopters crews to elevation the same day they arrive.
One itinerary contains your protocol; one deletes it.
That is the entire difference between them.
I sketched next week's plan for the ascent profiles before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the sampling plan updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
Both campaigns run the same weeks and pay identical field allowances.
The externals cancel out.
To the last line item.
The canyon lead keeps saying same-day insertion is how serious field teams operate now.
Seriousness framing.
Framing, and nothing else.
I closed the week by updating the field station handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Expedition sign-ups close Monday: plateau campaign or canyon campaign first on my list?
